# origincloud_compute_launch_template (Resource)

A recipe kept under a name: numbered versions of it, and the one that is the default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "origincloud_compute_key_pair" "admin" {
  project = "my-project-123"
}

# A recipe for instances. Changing launch_template_data adds a version, which
# becomes the default unless default_version is set: the versions that exist
# are never changed.
resource "origincloud_compute_launch_template" "web" {
  project = "my-project-123"
  tags    = { "origin:name" = "web" }

  launch_template_data = {
    instance_type = "//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/gp1.core.2"
    image_family  = "//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/ubuntu-24-04-minimal"
    key_pair      = origincloud_compute_key_pair.admin.id
    tags          = { role = "web" }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `launch_template_data` (Attributes) The recipe of the version this shows, `version`: the default version's unless the name named another. On creation, the recipe of version 1. Changing it adds a version; the launch template shows its newest. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--launch_template_data))
- `project` (String) The project the launch template is in. Changing it replaces the launch template.

### Optional

- `default_version` (Number) The number of the version launches use when they name no version. 1 on creation; an update sets it to another version the template has. Left out, it is the newest version after every change to `launch_template_data`, and what it was otherwise.
- `tags` (Map of String) Labels of your own for the launch template, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. The recipe's own `tags` are the instances'.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the launch template was created. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `creator` (String) The principal that created the launch template, by its full name on iam: `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/users/{user}`, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or a platform service agent's or service's name when the platform did.
- `id` (String) The launch template's full resource name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/launchTemplates/{launch_template}`: what an argument that refers to the launch template takes. `name` is the relative name, without the host.
- `latest_version` (Number) The number of the newest version the template has.
- `name` (String) The launch template's resource name. A template read at one version, by `@{version}`, `@default` or `@latest`, is named with that version's number, `projects/{project}/launchTemplates/{launch_template}@{version}`.
- `version` (Number) The number of the version whose recipe this shows.
- `version_create_time` (String) When that version was created. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.

<a id="nestedatt--launch_template_data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `launch_template_data`

Required:

- `instance_type` (String) The instance type by its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true.
- `key_pair` (String) The full name of the key pair whose public key is installed for `login_user`, in the launch's project.

Optional:

- `boot_volume` (Attributes) The boot volume's size and storage class. The image's size on the default storage class when left out. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--launch_template_data--boot_volume))
- `image` (String) The full name of the image the boot volume is created from, in the launch's zone: one of the project's own, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or a public one, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. Set exactly one of `image` and `image_family`.
- `image_family` (String) The full name of the image family to launch the current public image of, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Set exactly one of `image` and `image_family`.
- `local_disks` (Attributes List) Disks on the machine the instance runs on, beside its boot volume, created blank at launch; at most 16. A local disk is temporary: it comes back empty after every stop and start and after its machine restarts, and it is deleted with the instance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--launch_template_data--local_disks))
- `login_user` (String) The account to log in as: a user created at first boot that holds the key pair. A POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. The image's `default_user` when left empty.
- `network_interfaces` (Attributes List) The instance's network interfaces, in device order, the boot interface first; at most one today. Left empty, the instance gets one interface created from an empty spec: in the project's default subnet, with the VPC's default security group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--launch_template_data--network_interfaces))
- `service_account` (String) The full name of the service account the instance runs as, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`: a `WORKLOAD` service account of the project's organization that isn't deleted. Launching with one needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well. Empty for an instance that runs as none.
- `tags` (Map of String) Labels of your own for the instance, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows.

<a id="nestedatt--launch_template_data--boot_volume"></a>
### Nested Schema for `launch_template_data.boot_volume`

Optional:

- `size_gib` (Number) The size in GiB, at least the image's size; the image's size when left at 0. A smaller size is refused rather than raised.
- `storage_class` (String) The storage class by its full name, `//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/storageClasses/{storage_class}`; the default class when left empty.


<a id="nestedatt--launch_template_data--local_disks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `launch_template_data.local_disks`

Required:

- `size_gib` (Number) The size in GiB, at least 1.

Optional:

- `device` (String) The device name the guest sees the disk under, `vda` to `vdz` but `vdc`, and none the boot volume or another local disk has. The first free one, in the order the disks are listed, when left empty.


<a id="nestedatt--launch_template_data--network_interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `launch_template_data.network_interfaces`

Optional:

- `network_interface` (String) The full name of an existing interface, `//network.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/networkInterfaces/{network_interface}`, in the launch's project and zone, that nothing else holds. It brings its own subnet and security groups. Terminating the instance releases it, and it stays.
- `spec` (Attributes) An interface the launch creates for the instance. It is deleted when the instance is terminated; an instance that ends `FAILED` keeps it, so starting the instance again can use it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--launch_template_data--network_interfaces--spec))

<a id="nestedatt--launch_template_data--network_interfaces--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `launch_template_data.network_interfaces.spec`

Optional:

- `security_groups` (List of String) The full names of the security groups to put the interface in, `//network.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/securityGroups/{security_group}`, in the launch's project and region, in the subnet's VPC. Left empty, the VPC's default security group when it has one, and none when it has none: an interface in no security group admits and sends nothing but address resolution and replies to its own traffic.
- `subnet` (String) The full name of the subnet to create the interface in, `//network.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/subnets/{subnet}`, in the launch's project and zone. Left empty, the project's default subnet, in its default VPC: the first launch that needs them creates both, the VPC with an internet gateway attached and the subnet assigning each interface a public address. In a subnet that assigns public addresses, a launch whose address can't be assigned ends `FAILED` with the reason.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A launch template is imported by its full resource name, or its relative
# one, without a version: it is read at its newest.
terraform import origincloud_compute_launch_template.web //compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/my-project-123/launchTemplates/lt-1a2b3c
```
